questions.question: In modern microprocessor branch prediction architectures, why is a specialized Return Address Stack (RAS) implemented specifically for subroutine returns rather than relying on standard two-level adaptive branch history predictors?
options: Because a subroutine can be invoked from many distinct call sites across a program, making the return target address dependent on dynamic call nesting rather than local or global branch history patterns.
Because subroutine return instructions are unconditional branches that never evaluate to taken, rendering history tables redundant.
Because standard branch history tables cannot store 64-bit target addresses and are restricted to predicting single-bit branch directions.
Because the RAS eliminates the need for an instruction cache by pre-decoding the entire body of the target function into execution registers.
Because return instructions bypass the decode and rename pipeline stages, requiring target addresses to be supplied directly by the memory controller.

questions.question: In computer architecture, what is the primary operational distinction between Very Long Instruction Word (VLIW) architectures and superscalar architectures?
options: VLIW architectures rely entirely on dynamic runtime out-of-order execution hardware, whereas superscalar architectures strictly execute instructions in program order.

VLIW architectures rely on the compiler to statically identify instruction-level parallelism and bundle independent operations into a single wide instruction word, avoiding complex dynamic dependency-checking hardware.
VLIW architectures eliminate cache hierarchies by streaming wide instruction packets directly from off-chip main memory.
VLIW processors use a single unified execution unit that sequentially processes packed SIMD vectors, whereas superscalar processors duplicate ALUs.
VLIW architectures require extensive hardware register renaming and reorder buffers to dynamically resolve data hazards across multiple execution pipelines.

questions.question: In shared-memory multi-core computer architectures, what constitutes the performance pathology known as 'false sharing'?
options: Two threads simultaneously writing to the exact same memory word without synchronization, causing a non-deterministic race condition and data corruption.
A hardware thread mistakenly reading uncommitted speculative data from another thread's reorder buffer due to an alias in the store queue.

Multiple processor cores concurrently modifying completely independent variables that happen to reside within the same physical cache line, triggering frequent and unnecessary cache coherence invalidations.
Two distinct virtual memory pages mapping to the same set in a physically indexed cache, repeatedly evicting each other's data lines.
A failure in the directory-based coherence controller that erroneously marks a dirty cache line as clean in main memory.

questions.question: In low-power digital IC design employing power gating, what is the primary purpose of inserting isolation cells at the boundary between a power-gated domain and an always-on domain?
options: To step down the supply voltage level between higher-voltage core logic and lower-voltage I/O pads.
To store the complete architectural register state of the power-gated domain across the duration of the sleep cycle.
To prevent high-frequency clock jitter from coupling into sensitive analog and PLL power rails.
To clamp boundary signals to a known, valid logic level (0 or 1) when the domain is powered off, preventing floating inputs and excessive crowbar current in downstream always-on logic.
To filter out high-voltage ESD transients before they can degrade the gate oxide of input buffer transistors.

questions.question: In hardware networking devices and specialized memory design, what fundamental architectural capability distinguishes a Ternary Content-Addressable Memory (TCAM) from a conventional Binary CAM?
options: A TCAM uses three separate read/write ports to allow simultaneous lookup by three independent network processing cores.
A TCAM incorporates an internal three-state charge-pump mechanism to perform search operations at one-third the dynamic power of a binary CAM.
A TCAM stores data using three distinct voltage levels (ternary logic) within a single capacitive cell, tripling storage density relative to binary SRAM cells.
A TCAM outputs the exact physical memory address of every matching entry sequentially over three consecutive clock cycles.
Each storage bit in a TCAM supports a third 'don't care' (mask) state in addition to 0 and 1, enabling parallel wildcard searching and longest-prefix matching in a single clock cycle.
